In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of regulation of gene expression in the liver.
the isolation, characterization, and translation of messenger RNA from membrane-bound and nonbound polysomes of rabbit-liver.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the synthesis of specific proteins in mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane-bound and free RNA fractions are heterogeneous in terms of their translation in the heterologus reticulocyte protein synthesizing system.
, under the conditions used in the reticuocyte cell-free system, there is no distinction in the relative percentage synthesis of albumin or ferritin in membrane-bound versus free polysomes.

, in addition to a large portion of the messenger RNA which is translated in a cell-free system, there is a significant amount of messenger RNA which is not translated in such systems, but is translated when the RNA is reconstituted into a polysomal system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in addition to a small portion of messenger RNA that can be translated in a heterologous system, membrane-bound polysomes also contain a significant portion of RNA with messenger activity that cannot be translated in the hetero- logous system but is capable of directing the synthesis of specific proteins in homologous polysomes.
the membrane-bound polysome fraction of rabbit liver is a more complex mixture than previously thought, containing both membrane-bound and cytoplasmic messenger RNA.
the messenger activity in membrane-bound and in free polysomes is not exclusively confined to albumin and ferrin, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that there is evidence of nontranslated messenger RNA in membrane bound polysomes and free polysomes from rabbit liver.
the cell-free system is not a perfect mimic of what happens in a live cell.

, in the rabbit reticulocyte lysate system, there are significant differences in protein synthesis from membrane-bound versus free polysomes, but these differences are not due to differences in the relative amount of messenger RNA for albumin and ferritins in these polysome fractions.
